Risk-based Premium Framework for Deposit Insurance in India Based on a comprehensive review, DICGC has, with the approval of the Reserve Bank, decided to implement a Risk Based Premium (RBP) Framework with effect from April 1,2026, in terms of the provision under Section 15(1) of the DICGC Act, 1961 which provides for differential premium rates for different categories of insured banks.

# Page 4^page=4
Background Since 1962, the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) has been operating the deposit insurance scheme Since inception, DICGC has levied a flat rate premium to fund the scheme. At present, banks are charged a premium of 12 paise per ₹100 of assessable deposits (AD) per annum (paid on half-yearly basis), regardless of how well or poorly the bank manages its risks.

# Page 5^page=5
Risk-based Premium Framework for Deposit Insurance in India Based on a comprehensive review, DICGC has, with the approval of the Reserve Bank, decided to implement a Risk Based Premium (RBP) Framework with effect from April 1,2026, in terms of the provision under Section 15(1)of the DICGC Act, 1961 which provides for differential premium rates for different categories of insured banks. The RBP Framework incentivises sound risk management by banks and facilitates better managed banks to pay a lower premium than the Card Rate of 12 paise per ₹100 of AD per annum. Enforcement: The RBP framework shall be effective from April 1, 2026, and will be reviewed at least once in three years.

# Page 6^page=6
Risk Based Rating Methodology The RBP Framework includes a two tier Risk Based Rating Methodology Local Area Bank (LABs) and Payments Banks (PBs) will continue to pay the card rate (i.e., 12 paise per ₹100 of AD per annum) as there are data point limitations to bring them into a Risk Based Pricing model. In tier 1 - For small foreign banks and for Small Finance Banks (SFBs), weightage of supervisory ratings will be shifted to quantitative assessment.

# Page 7^page=7
Rating categorisation and Risk Based Premium Based on the risk assessment score obtained by the Corporation, each bank will be categorised into four groups - Category A, B, C, or D for the purpose of determining the applicable premium rate. Category A includes the safest banks, while Category D includes the riskiest ones. Earlier, all banks paid the flat insurance premium of 12 paise for every ₹100 of deposits, no matter how safe or risky they were. Now, the amount they pay depends on their risk category. Discount\Risk Model incentive available to safest bank is 33.33% of the card rate, which represents the highest permissible reduction in premium for eligible banks.

# Page 8^page=8
Vintage Incentive - This rewards long-standing banks with a clean track record. ln the event of restructuring or major distress - Vintage Incentive calculated from the date of restructuring/distress End-date of previous FY considered for computing vintage incentive RBP framework also provide benefits of vintage - Banks are rewarded for long-term stable operations without major stress or restructuring. This reflects their longer contribution to the Deposit Insurance Fund. Vintage Incentive - Tier 1 Banks - 1% premium discount for each completed year Maximum 25% discount for banks operating 25 years or more No record of restructuring or major distress Vintage Inc. - Tier 2 Banks (Applicable to RRBs, StCBs, DCCBs & Tier 4 UCBs) Flat 25% premium discount; If bank has completed 25 years of satisfactory conduct No restructuring or major distress during the period The vintage incentive is given over and above the Risk Model incentive.

# Page 10^page=10
Rating Override Policy •DICGC retains the right to override the rating as per its Board-approved policy. •An override may be exercised if: o Adverse information is reported by the banking supervisor, or o DICGC’s own assessment identifies material risk concerns. •ln such cases, concerned bank will be required to pay such premium as assessed by DICGC from the next HY, until it returns to normalcy in the assessment of DICGC.

# Page 11^page=11
Disclosure Policy • Risk rating category will be communicated confidentially to the MD/CEO of the insured bank. • The applicable premium (based on the effective premium rate) will be available on DICGC’s ‘Samyak’ Portal at the start of the payment cycle. • Banks must not disclose or use the risk category for business solicitation. • Violation may invite penal action by DICGC/RBI/NABARD. • Premium must be paid as per Section 19(1) of DICGC Regulations, 1961. • Payment timeline: After commencement of the half-year, But not later than the last day of the second month of that half-year. Payment to be made through the ‘Samyak’ Portal. Half Year Period 2026 - 27 Deposit Base Used Last Date for Payment 1st HY April–September Deposits as on March 31, 2026 May 31 2nd HY October–March Deposits as on Sept 30, 2026 November 30

Base Year = 2018. The index for September 2025 stands at 516.76 as against 493.22 for March 2025.

RBI – Digital Payments Index for September 2025 The increase in RBI-DPI index was driven by significant growth in parameters viz. Payment Performance and Payment Enablers across the country over the period. The RBI-DPI has been constructed with March 2018 as the base period, i.e. DPI score for March 2018 is set at 100. Going forward, RBI-DPI shall be published on RBI’s website on a semi- annual basis from March 2021 onwards with a lag of 4 months.

Q1. With reference to the Risk Based Rating Model under the Risk Based Premium (RBP) Framework, consider the following statements: 1. Tier 1 Model is applicable to all Scheduled Commercial Banks including Regional Rural Banks (RRBs). 2. Risk rating under Tier 1 employs supervisory ratings of the Reserve Bank of India, quantitative assessment, and potential loss to the Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF). 3. Local Area Banks (LABs) and Payments Banks (PBs) will continue to pay the card rate due to data limitations. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? (A) 1 only (B) 2 only (C) 2 and 3 only (D) 1 and 3 only (E) 1, 2 and 3 MCQs for Practice
